Dumbbell Back Row Variations Guide

A focused upper body tutorial demonstrating how different elbow angles and hand positions shift activation across the middle back, upper back, lower lats, and erector spinae during dumbbell bent-over rows.

10–15 min
Duration
4
Exercises

Exercise Flow

Check off each exercise as you complete sets. Rest timer at the bottom.
01

Dumbbell Middle Back Row

3 × 10–12 reps
RhomboidsMiddle TrapeziusLatissimus Dorsi
  • Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back
  • Flare elbows at approximately 45 degrees and pull toward your mid-torso

Why: Targets the rhomboids and mid-traps to build overall back thickness and posture.

02

Wide-Elbow Dumbbell Row

3 × 10–12 reps
Upper TrapeziusRear DeltoidsRhomboids
  • Flare elbows out wide at roughly 90 degrees
  • Pull dumbbells up toward the upper chest level

Why: Shifts emphasis to the rear deltoids and upper traps for complete upper back development.

03

Close-Grip Lat Row

3 × 10–12 reps
Latissimus DorsiLower Trapezius
  • Keep elbows tucked tightly against your torso
  • Pull dumbbells back towards your hip pockets

Why: Maximizes lower lat contraction to enhance back width and V-taper structure.

04

Single-Arm Dumbbell Bent-Over Row

3 × 10–12 reps per side
Erector SpinaeLatissimus DorsiCore
  • Support your torso position while rowing one dumbbell
  • Drive elbow upward and squeeze your back while maintaining core alignment

Why: Isolates back muscles unilaterally while engaging spinal erectors and core stability.

Trainer Tips

  • Adjusting your elbow angle relative to your torso changes muscle recruitment across the back.
  • Maintain a neutral spine and engaged core throughout all bent-over row variations.
